comparison: Both evaluations support the experimental design and methodology (C13-C14, C65-C72). OpenEval notes appropriate sample sizes for baseline cohort with acknowledgment of smaller MDMA cohort. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the study design as 'convincing' with 'solid study design.' High agreement on methodological soundness.

Both support the baseline MC and FC characterization (C15-C17, C38-C39, C58-C59). OpenEval emphasizes statistical appropriateness and complementary nature of modalities. Peer reviewers described methods as 'highly novel and powerful' and 'convincing.' Strong agreement on feasibility and reliability of the approach.

OpenEval supports temporal stability findings (C18) with detailed analysis of both modalities. Peer review R2 includes C18 in broader baseline characterization but does not specifically address temporal stability. Partial overlap with general acceptance of baseline methods.

Both address ICA results (C19-C21, C40-C42). OpenEval supports findings with acknowledgment of lower PET temporal resolution. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting 'fMRI ICs appear fairly restricted' and questioning bilateral patterns in PET ICs, suggesting methodological limitations may affect network patterns. Divergence in confidence level.

Both support the baseline MC prediction of MDMA response (C22-C23, C60). OpenEval notes high significance but acknowledges small MDMA cohort as limitation. Peer reviewers found results 'quite intriguing' and accepted temporal dynamics without critique. Agreement on biological relevance despite sample size concerns.

Both support MC versus BPND comparison (C24-C25, C61-C62). OpenEval emphasizes complementary information and network-level changes. Peer reviewers accepted differential sensitivity as demonstrating MC's enhanced utility. Strong agreement on MC providing information beyond traditional measures.

OpenEval expresses UNCERTAINTY about differential MC/FC sensitivity to MDMA (C26-C28, C43, C49, C52), citing lack of FDR correction and small sample size. Peer reviewers SUPPORT these findings, affirming 'more pronounced alterations in MC than in FC' as a key finding. Significant divergence in evaluation confidence.

Both support mechanistic interpretations from literature (C29-C37). OpenEval notes these are interpretive claims not directly testable by current data. Peer reviewers accepted these as part of theoretical framework without critique. Agreement on appropriateness of literature-based discussion.

OpenEval expresses UNCERTAINTY about hierarchical mechanism speculation (C44-C45), noting claims are speculative and not definitively established. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the interpretation, finding temporal effects 'quite intriguing' and accepting it as reasonable speculation. Moderate divergence in confidence.

Both support contextualization within existing literature (C46-C48). OpenEval notes C49 weakens direct comparison due to trend-level findings. Peer reviewers accepted alignment with previous findings without question. General agreement with minor caveat from OpenEval.

OpenEval supports main contributions (C50-C51, C64) as methodological advance. Peer review R9 supports complementary nature of MC and FC (C64, C38-C39, C59) as 'highly novel and powerful.' Agreement on significance of contributions, though addressing partially overlapping claim sets.

Both address anesthesia limitations (C53-C55, C69). OpenEval supports transparent acknowledgment with partial validation from prior work. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting 'high anaesthetic dose used likely limiting network activity' and 'suboptimal anaesthetic regimen.' Agreement on limitation existence, slight divergence on impact assessment.

Both address small MDMA sample size (C56-C57). OpenEval supports transparent acknowledgment but notes C57's consistency argument doesn't substitute for adequate power. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, specifically concerned about replicability and requesting additional justification. Agreement on limitation, with peer review showing stronger concern.

Both support acknowledgment of mechanistic uncertainty (C63). OpenEval emphasizes this honest assessment strengthens credibility. Peer reviewers accepted this as appropriate acknowledgment of methodological boundaries. Complete agreement on this limitation.

OpenEval supports comprehensive methodological details (C73-C88) as appropriate and reproducible. Peer review R1 includes C73 in broader methodological acceptance. Minimal overlap but general agreement on methodological soundness where claims intersect.
OpenEval supports background and research gap identification (C1-C12) as justified by literature review. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.
